faq.a: Abdullah represents Arabic عَبْدُ الله, meaning servant of God/Allah.

faq.q: What is the origin of Abdullah?
faq.a: The name is Arabic and is a compound of عبد and a second element.
Yes. The underlying compound is عَبْدُ الله (ʿAbd Allāh).

faq.q: What is the root of Abdullah?
faq.a: عبد is related to ع ب د; the second element is Allah.
Abdullah is a traditional Muslim personal name; the meaning comes from the complete compound.
This record does not establish Abdullah as an explicitly named Qur'anic person; a phrase or divine epithet is distinct from personal-name attestation in the text.

faq.q: What does Abdullah mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, the name means servant of God/Allah; the compound combines عبد with Allah.
The supplied “ab-dul-lah” is an approximate pronunciation; local pronunciations vary.

faq.q: Is Abdullah a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: The record classifies the name as masculine, consistent with traditional usage; regional frequency data is not supplied.
